package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to covertly collect sensitive payment card and personal information from checkout forms on restaurant ordering platforms and exfiltrate it to attacker-controlled domains. This constitutes credential theft and payment card fraud.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when checkout page is loaded and user enters data)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into checkout page HTML/JavaScript (e.g., main.js, inline <script> tag)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user clicks the checkout button, the code collects credit card number, expiration month/year, CVV2, and billing address from the form fields, then exfiltrates this data to a remote attacker-controlled domain via a dynamically created script tag.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code surreptitiously collects sensitive payment data from form fields and sends it to an external domain unrelated to the legitimate payment processor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal checkout scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment gateways via secure POST requests, not via script tags to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment integrations may collect form data, but only transmit to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: Access to payment form fields (CC_number, cc_month, cc_year, cc_cvv2, CC_address)
Use of dynamically created script tag for data exfiltration

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when checkout page is loaded and user enters data)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into MenuDrive platform checkout page (separate script)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user submits the checkout form, the code collects the cardholder's name, email, phone number, and payment card details, then exfiltrates this data via an HTTP POST request to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script collects both personal and payment data and sends it to an external, non-legitimate endpoint.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should only transmit sensitive data to the payment processor or backend, not to unknown third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment integrations may collect similar data, but only for processing payments with trusted providers.
key_indicators: Collection of PII and payment data
Use of fetch/XHR to send data externally

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user interacts with fake payment form)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into InTouchPOS platform checkout page (fake form overlay)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code overlays a fake payment form on the checkout page, collects all entered payment and user data, and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled server when the form is submitted.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script creates a fake payment form to phish user data, which is then sent to an external domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout pages should not overlay fake forms or intercept user data for external transmission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; overlaying fake forms is inherently malicious.
key_indicators: Creation of new form elements over existing UI

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the checkout page of restaurant ordering platforms.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of sensitive payment and personal data from users.

attack_chain.action: When a user enters payment details and submits the form, the malicious script collects the data from the DOM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of collected data to attacker-controlled domains.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is exfiltrated to external domains via HTTP requests or dynamically created script tags.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives payment card and PII, enabling carding and fraud.

attack_chain.action: Stolen payment card data is sold on dark web marketplaces.
attack_chain.leads_to: Financial fraud and loss for victims.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript accessing payment form fields (credit card, CVV, expiration, address, name, email, phone)
Exfiltration of form data to external domains via fetch/XHR or dynamically created script tags
Creation of new form overlays or fake forms on checkout pages
file_indicators: Unexpected inline <script> tags on checkout pages
References to suspicious domains (e.g., authorizen.net, malicious-domain.com)
Injected scripts not present in original platform codebase
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains such as authorizen.net/ord.php or other non-standard endpoints during checkout
POST requests containing payment or PII data to unknown domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected JavaScript accessing payment form fields and sending data to external domains. Scan for inline or injected scripts on checkout pages, especially those referencing suspicious domains. Use web application firewalls (WAF) and content security policies (CSP) to block unauthorized script execution and outbound requests. Regularly audit subdomains and web assets for unauthorized code changes.
